It isn’t a garden spray; something that pure is only in our cabinet, a standard vial for residue tests. Yesterday morning I counted; one vial was missing. The cabinet key is with me and the manager. I didn’t tell anyone; I was scared.
She takes off her glasses and wipes them on the hem of her lab coat.
Where does the chemical you found in the coffee come from?
I measure samples.
Anabel Ríos — interview

A file reopened from the archive (March 1999, closed as a ‘workplace accident’):

· Antonio Heredia (44), on the fourth day of the strike, was crushed under a reversing forklift in the packing house. In the accident log: ‘His own carelessness; the forklift was parked.’
· That page of the log was scraped and rewritten; forensic examination shows the original entry began ‘the forklift was running, driver’. The page was signed by the deputy manager, Beatriz Soto.
· Manuel Ortega is on the witness list; his statement was never taken.
· In 2000 the cooperative’s land was sold to the Fundación Santa Ana; adviser’s signature ‘E. V.’
The file closed as a ‘workplace accident’ thirty-one years ago has been reopened.
THE 1999 FILE — ANTONIO HEREDIA

· Cause of death: organophosphate poisoning; respiratory arrest.
· Coffee and a high concentration of the chemical in the stomach; the chemical itself is an odourless laboratory standard, purer than garden spray.
· No chemical on the skin: not picked up from spraying in the grove.
· Poison ingested: 13.00–13.20.
AUTOPSY REPORT
Cooperative manager.
The cooperative supports two hundred families; think of them.
No.
I was twenty-three. The one driving the forklift was the manager’s son; they told me, ‘Fix the log, or the cooperative goes under.’ I fixed it. Later I became manager.

On Friday Manolo was going to tell Esteban. Thirty-one years, two hundred families, the land sale, the foundation… It would all come out. I took the vial from the cabinet and emptied it into the thermos. I couldn’t throw the empty vial away; I left it in the car. How stupid.
You emptied the vial from the cabinet into Manolo’s thermos.
I’m the manager; I go everywhere. But what would I want with a thermos? Manolo was old, forty years in a sprayed grove. One day it was bound to happen.
She pulls the zip of her gilet up a finger’s width.
Did you go into the canteen this morning?
Beatriz Soto — interview
Cooperative canteen, lockers and shelf. 22 October 07.30 – 13.10.
CANTEEN CAMERA — log transcript

Beatriz Soto’s car and her office at the cooperative (with the branch chief’s approval):

· In the driver’s door pocket, the standard vial missing from the lab cabinet; inside, a few drops of the same chemical as in the coffee, and Beatriz Soto’s fingerprint on the vial.
· In the safe in her office, the original copy of the 1999 accident log, unscraped: ‘The forklift was running, driver: R. Morales.’
· On her phone, 21 October, to an unregistered number: ‘Ortega will talk on Friday.’ No reply.

Beatriz Soto was arrested; the 1999 file was reopened as ‘negligent homicide and forgery of an official document’. Thirty-one years on, Esteban Heredia had the true date carved on his father’s grave for the first time.

I was nineteen. On the fourth day of the strike he was crushed under a forklift in the packing house. ‘His own carelessness,’ they said; that’s what the log said. I’ve fought this cooperative for thirty years; everyone knows. But who would harm Manolo? He was the only man I had left from my father. At noon I was in a meeting, with ten people.

On the afternoon of 22 October 2030, in the grove of the Cooperativa Naranjos del Sur outside Sevilla, the picker Manuel Ortega (66) collapsed during his lunch break and died before reaching hospital. The cooperative’s lab found an organophosphate insecticide in the coffee in his thermos.

At the cooperative that day: manager Beatriz Soto, pickers’ representative Esteban Heredia, picker Karim Ouazzani, lab technician Anabel Ríos. The victim’s neighbour Dolores Vega called the ambulance.

The technician told of the missing vial, the neighbour of Manolo’s last words; those got the archive opened. The camera showed the woman who touched the thermos. The search found the vial in the car and the original log in the safe.
She had fixed the log once; the second time, coffee was enough.
Naranjos del Sur — October 2030

In the 1999 strike a forklift crushed the strike leader Antonio Heredia; the deputy manager Beatriz Soto rewrote the accident log as ‘his own carelessness’ and years later became manager. Thirty-one years on, the picker Manolo Ortega, who had been there that day, decided to tell the leader’s son. Beatriz took the vial of pure chemical from the lab cabinet, emptied it into Manolo’s thermos in the canteen in the morning and left the empty vial in her car.
Who killed Manuel Ortega?
